newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK activists to fly to Japan in islands dispute.
newsitem.headline: HK activists to fly to Japan in islands dispute.

text.p: Two Hong Kong legislators supporting China's claim to a group of disputed islands in the East China Sea will fly to Japan on Thursday in a bid to pressure Tokyo into backing down from its rival claim.
Members of the 123 Democratic Alliance in Hong Kong plan to meet officials from Japan's foreign ministry on April 21, said chairman Yum Sin-ling, who is also a legislator.
"We want the Japanese government to return the Diaoyu islands, and we want to declare that they belong to China," Yum said.
He will leave for Japan on Thursday with another group member and fellow legislator Mak Yip-sing. Both men plan to return to Hong Kong on April 22.

Known as the Diaoyu in Chinese and Senkaku in Japanese, the cluster of uninhabited rocky outcrops have kindled fiery passions among Chinese communities since Japanese rightwingers built a lighthouse and planted flags there in July last year.
